title: Dead letters can be stored but not managed: ISyncManager exposes no retry or resolution API even though the storage layer has remove and removeByRemote
content:
The reactor's own open-issue list records this as gap 4a. `KyselySyncDeadLetterStorage` implements `remove(id)` and `removeByRemote()`, but **`ISyncManager` has no methods for dead-letter management**, so nothing above the storage layer can retry or resolve one.

The consequence for an operator: a document that dead-letters is quarantined until someone reaches past the sync manager into storage. There is no supported "retry this dead letter" call, no way to drain a remote's dead letters as a batch through the public interface, and therefore no UI that can offer it without depending on storage internals.

This pairs badly with the one failure mode that is guaranteed *not* to converge on its own — two reactors writing conflicting auth-scope operations, where the replica whose stream ran ahead dead-letters the arrival and holds a different policy until an application reconciles it. The reconciliation the design assumes has no interface to perform it through.
